newsitem.title: USA: Enron revises terms of Portland General acquisition.
newsitem.headline: Enron revises terms of Portland General acquisition.

text.p: Enron Corp. said Monday it revised the terms of its proposed $2.1 billion acquisition of Portland General Corp. by increasing customer benefits and lowering the payout to Portland General shareholders.
Enron said it would increase customer benefits by $141 million but lower the ratio to 0.9825-for-one from one-for-one at which shares would be paid to Portland shareholders.

The revision comes in response to the decision announced Friday by the Oregon Public Utility Commission to recommend that Enron's acquisition of Portland General be denied unless the companies come up with rate reductions of at least $141 million for Portland's electric utility customers.

Portland General's stock closed at $35.125, up $3.125, and Enron's stock closed at $37.50, up $1.625, both on the New York Stock Exchange. At that price, Portland General's shareholders would receive $36.84 a share and the deal would be worth $1.89 billion.
